title: Operational Amplifier

precautions.title: ⚡ Supply Rail Voltage Limits
precautions.description: Do not exceed ±15V on the Vcc (+V) and Vee (-V) pins of the IC 741. Reversing polarity or exceeding absolute maximum ratings (±22V) will cause immediate thermal destruction of the semiconductor junctions.

precautions.title: 🔌 Input Overdrive / Saturation
precautions.description: Ensure the input signal voltage (Vin) combined with circuit gain does not demand an output voltage exceeding the supply rails. The Op-Amp will saturate, causing signal clipping and distortion.

theory.title: 📖 Theory — Operational Amplifier Characteristics
theory.objective: To study the voltage gain, input/output characteristics, and saturation limits of an operational amplifier (IC 741) in inverting and non-inverting configurations.
points: An operational amplifier is a high-gain differential amplifier with very high input impedance and very low output impedance.
In the inverting configuration, the input signal is applied to the inverting (-) terminal through an input resistor R₁, with feedback resistor Rf connecting output to inverting input.
In the non-inverting configuration, the input signal is applied directly to the non-inverting (+) terminal, with the feedback network connected to the inverting terminal.
The output voltage is limited by the supply rails (±Vcc). When the theoretical output exceeds these limits, the amplifier saturates and clips the signal.

formulaDetails.name: Inverting Amplifier Gain

variables.name: Closed-Loop Voltage Gain
variables.desc: Ratio of output voltage to input voltage

variables.name: Feedback Resistor
variables.desc: Resistor connecting output to inverting input

variables.name: Input Resistor
variables.desc: Resistor connecting signal source to inverting input

formulaDetails.description: The negative sign indicates 180° phase inversion between input and output. Gain magnitude is set entirely by the resistor ratio.
formulaDetails.physicalSignificance: Provides predictable, stable gain independent of the op-amp's open-loop characteristics.

formulaDetails.name: Non-Inverting Amplifier Gain

variables.name: Closed-Loop Voltage Gain
variables.desc: Ratio of output voltage to input voltage

variables.name: Ground Resistor
variables.desc: Resistor connecting inverting input to ground

formulaDetails.description: Output is in-phase with input (no phase inversion). Minimum gain is unity (when Rf = 0 or R₁ = ∞).
formulaDetails.physicalSignificance: Used when signal polarity must be preserved, such as in voltage followers and buffer circuits.

procedure: Select the Op-Amp mode (Inverting or Non-Inverting).
Set the feedback resistor (Rf) and input resistor (Rin).
Apply the DC input voltage (Vin) within the limits of the supply rails (±15V).
Observe the output voltage (Vout) on the multimeter.
Compare the theoretical Vout with the observed Vout and note any saturation clipping.

viva: What is the concept of Virtual Ground in an Op-Amp?

In an inverting configuration with feedback, the inverting terminal is kept at approximately 0V by the amplifier because the non-inverting terminal is grounded, despite having no physical connection to ground.
The output voltage cannot exceed the DC supply voltage rails (+Vcc and -Vee). If the input times the gain demands a higher voltage, the signal clips (saturates).
